Seasonal demand profile for short-stay places

Source: R/seasonal_demand.R
seasonal_demand.Rd

Works out how busy each place is in each calendar month, using guest reviews as a stand-in for bookings. Demand is shown as an index where 1 is that place's own average month, so a small town and the Melbourne CBD can sit on the same chart. A value of 2 means a month is twice as busy as usual for that place, and 0.5 means half as busy.

Usage

seasonal_demand(
  places,
  stay_type = "Short stay (under 28 nights)",
  room_type = "Entire home/apt",
  baseline = "Melbourne CBD",
  reviews = staysvic::vic_reviews_monthly
)

Arguments

places

Character vector of place names from vic_places or the place column of vic_listings, for example c("Lorne", "Sorrento").

stay_type

Which listings to count. One of "Short stay (under 28 nights)" (the default), "Mid stay (28 nights or more)" or "All".

room_type

One of "Entire home/apt" (the default), "Private room", "Hotel room", "Shared room" or "All".

baseline

A place that is always included for comparison. Defaults to "Melbourne CBD". Use NULL to leave it out.

reviews

Monthly review counts. Defaults to vic_reviews_monthly.

Value

A tibble with one row per place and calendar month, containing place, month (1 to 12), month_label, avg_reviews (average reviews in that month across years), index (the month compared with the place's average month), total_reviews (all reviews for the place in the data) and enough_data (TRUE when there are at least 100 reviews, which keeps one busy weekend from looking like a trend).

Details

Months are averaged across every year in the data, so each calendar month appears about three times.

Examples

seasonal_demand(c("Lorne", "Apollo Bay"))
#> # A tibble: 36 × 7
#>    place         month month_label avg_reviews index total_reviews enough_data
#>    <chr>         <int> <fct>             <dbl> <dbl>         <int> <lgl>      
#>  1 Melbourne CBD     1 Jan               6413. 1.08         214262 TRUE       
#>  2 Melbourne CBD     2 Feb               5705  0.959        214262 TRUE       
#>  3 Melbourne CBD     3 Mar               6332  1.06         214262 TRUE       
#>  4 Melbourne CBD     4 Apr               5653  0.950        214262 TRUE       
#>  5 Melbourne CBD     5 May               5363  0.901        214262 TRUE       
#>  6 Melbourne CBD     6 Jun               5465. 0.918        214262 TRUE       
#>  7 Melbourne CBD     7 Jul               6244. 1.05         214262 TRUE       
#>  8 Melbourne CBD     8 Aug               6247. 1.05         214262 TRUE       
#>  9 Melbourne CBD     9 Sep               6342  1.07         214262 TRUE       
#> 10 Melbourne CBD    10 Oct               5709. 0.959        214262 TRUE       
#> # ℹ 26 more rows

# Peak month for each place
prof <- seasonal_demand(c("Lorne", "Sorrento"))
prof[prof$index == ave(prof$index, prof$place, FUN = max), ]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   place         month month_label avg_reviews index total_reviews enough_data
#>   <chr>         <int> <fct>             <dbl> <dbl>         <int> <lgl>      
#> 1 Melbourne CBD     1 Jan               6413.  1.08        214262 TRUE       
#> 2 Lorne             1 Jan                344   1.29          9566 TRUE       
#> 3 Sorrento          1 Jan                281.  1.5           6736 TRUE
